name: Megestrol acetate

lead: Megestrol acetate is a prescription progestin used for advanced breast and endometrial cancer and for anorexia or wasting in people with AIDS. It stimulates appetite and is sometimes mentioned as a weight-gain drug.

All of its published weight-gain evidence comes from sick populations such as people with cancer or HIV. Reviews describe limited and low-quality evidence in elderly patients, and no trials have tested it in healthy people seeking cosmetic weight gain.

paras: It activates progesterone receptors, suppresses gonadotropins and has some glucocorticoid activity. How it raises appetite is not fully understood; proposed routes include neuropeptide Y, reduced inflammatory cytokines and IGF-1.

Documented risks include fluid retention, blood clots, adrenal suppression, lowered sex hormones, bone loss and fetal harm. It is prescription-only in the US and most countries, and the manufacturer of its branded suspension settled a 2013 lawsuit over off-label promotion.

lead: Megestrol acetate is a synthetic progestin, a laboratory-made relative of the hormone progesterone, sold mainly under the brand name Megace. It is a prescription drug used to treat advanced breast and endometrial cancer and, in an oral suspension form, anorexia, cachexia or unexplained significant weight loss in people with AIDS [1][2]. Its appetite-stimulating effect is the reason it appears in discussions of weight gain.

In appearance-focused settings the drug is relevant only as an appetite stimulant, a category of medicines some people consider when trying to gain weight. Published trials of megestrol for weight gain have been conducted in people with cancer cachexia and HIV-related wasting, not in healthy people seeking cosmetic change. A reference summary notes that studies in elderly patients with weight loss are limited and mostly show little or no weight gain [2].

Documented adverse effects include fluid retention, vaginal bleeding, thromboembolic events, adrenal suppression with glucocorticoid-like effects, and suppression of sex hormones; it is contraindicated in pregnancy [1][2].

paras: In oncology the drug is used for palliative treatment of advanced breast cancer and endometrial cancer [2][3]. The US label for the oral suspension lists treatment of anorexia, cachexia or unexplained significant weight loss in patients with AIDS [1]. It has also been used off-label for hot flashes, endometriosis and other conditions [2][4]. Veterinary versions are used to suppress estrus in dogs and cats [2].

No regulator has approved megestrol for cosmetic weight gain or body-composition change, and no published trial has tested it for that purpose in healthy people. Its relevance to looksmaxxing is as one of several appetite stimulants that people exploring weight gain may read about, alongside antihistamines such as cyproheptadine.

In cancer and AIDS cachexia, megestrol is reported to increase appetite in many patients, but the effect on body composition differs from lean-tissue gain: reviews of cachexia describe weight loss as a mix of fat and muscle wasting driven by cytokines and altered metabolism [5][6]. A reference summary states that very high doses substantially raise appetite and that evidence in elderly patients with weight loss is limited and of poor quality, with most studies showing minimal weight gain and no clear clinical benefit [2].

A North Central Cancer Treatment Group trial compared dronabinol, megestrol acetate and their combination for cancer-associated anorexia [7]. In breast cancer, randomized trials found newer aromatase inhibitors (letrozole, exemestane) more effective and better tolerated than megestrol as second-line therapy [8][9]. Megestrol has also been studied for hot flashes [10] and, with other agents, for fertility-sparing treatment of endometrial hyperplasia [11].

The US label notes that megestrol may cause fetal harm and advises women of childbearing potential to avoid pregnancy [1]. Reference sources list weight gain, edema, nausea, vaginal bleeding, dizziness and shortness of breath as common effects; thromboembolic events including deep vein thrombosis; hypogonadism and sexual dysfunction; osteoporosis; and, at high doses, glucocorticoid-like effects such as Cushing-like symptoms, steroid diabetes and adrenal insufficiency [2]. The Wikipedia article reports that a study of older patients found serious adverse events leading to death in a small proportion [2].

Megestrol acetate is a progesterone-receptor agonist that also suppresses gonadotropins, lowering sex-hormone levels, and has some glucocorticoid-receptor activity [2][12]. The mechanism of the appetite effect is not fully understood; proposed contributors include neuropeptide Y, reduced inflammatory cytokines, glucocorticoid-like action and increased IGF-1 [2]. Oral bioavailability is high and food increases absorption of the suspension [2]. The mean elimination half-life is reported as about 34 hours [2].

The compound was synthesized in 1959 and introduced in 1963 as a component of an oral contraceptive; contraceptive combinations were withdrawn from some markets in the early 1970s after reports of thromboembolism and animal tumor findings [2][13]. It entered US use for endometrial cancer in 1971, and the oral suspension was approved for AIDS-related anorexia and cachexia in 1993 [2]. In 2013 the manufacturer Par Pharmaceutical settled a US federal and state lawsuit alleging promotion of Megace ES for non-AIDS geriatric wasting, a use not approved by the FDA [2].

No studies have tested megestrol acetate for weight gain or appearance goals in healthy people. Human trials address cancer, AIDS-related and other medical wasting, breast and endometrial cancer, and hot flashes [1][5][7][8][9][10].

Registered trials include a phase 3 study of megestrol for weight loss during neoadjuvant chemotherapy in colorectal cancer, recruiting as of 2025 [14], and pharmacokinetic studies of the concentrated suspension and food effects [15][16]. Several registered trials in endometrial hyperplasia and cancer were terminated early [17][18].

timeline.event: Megestrol acetate is synthesized at Syntex [2].
Introduced in the UK as an oral contraceptive component [2].
Introduced in the US for endometrial cancer [2].
